headline: Software Surge Steals the Show as Consumer Names Buckle Under Pressure
body_html:
Thursday's session belonged squarely to enterprise software and cybersecurity, as a wave of earnings-driven enthusiasm swept through technology while the rest of the market struggled to keep pace. Of the 549 names in our universe, decliners outnumbered advancers 294 to 252, underscoring that the day's gains were concentrated rather than broad — a tape carried by a handful of high-conviction moves, not a rising tide.

The sector rotation told a clear story: Software led all groups with a 3.0% advance, Semiconductors added 1.72%, and Energy climbed 1.58% — the latter buoyed by ongoing tensions surrounding Iran's Strait of Hormuz posture and the knock-on effect of elevated fuel prices. Meanwhile, Consumer fell 1.17% and Homebuilders shed 1.74%, reflecting a market quietly pricing in a more cautious household spending outlook heading into autumn.

The standout mover of the session was Okta, which surged 28.63% — an emphatic single-day rerating that capped a remarkable afternoon for identity and security software broadly. Salesforce and CrowdStrike added 22.58% and 20.50%, respectively, signaling that investors believe the worst of the enterprise spending drought may be behind the cohort. Whether Thursday's enthusiasm holds into Friday will depend in large part on tone from Washington and any fresh developments overseas.

briefs.headline: Okta's Historic Single-Session Jump Resets the Identity-Security Conversation
briefs.body: Okta surged 28.63% on Thursday, its largest single-session advance in recent memory, after results apparently demolished lingering doubts about customer retention and growth durability. The move dragged peers higher across the identity and access-management space, reinforcing a broader view that security software budgets remain largely intact even as corporate belts tighten elsewhere.

briefs.headline: Iran Strait Conditions Rattle Energy Markets, Lift Oil-Linked Equities
briefs.body: A senior Iranian security official outlined conditions under which Tehran might reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping energy traders on edge and supporting crude-linked equities for a second consecutive session. The Energy sector finished up 1.58% in our universe. Reports also indicate the White House is convening refiners and fuel retailers to address gasoline-price pressure ahead of the midterm cycle.

briefs.headline: Prediction Markets Take Center Stage Ahead of Warsh Remarks
briefs.body: Market participants are closely watching forecasting platforms for clues on how Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh's upcoming public remarks may land with investors. Prediction-market signals have become an increasingly cited input on Wall Street for gauging policy tone, and Thursday's chatter suggested a wide range of possible interpretations depending on his precise language.

briefs.headline: Burlington and Celsius Lead Consumer Retreat as Spending Worries Deepen
briefs.body: Burlington Stores dropped 7.64% and Celsius Holdings fell 6.36%, two of the steeper single-name declines in Thursday's session. The moves reinforced a day-long drag on the Consumer sector, which finished down 1.17%, as investors appeared to question whether discretionary and beverage names can sustain volume growth against a backdrop of elevated fuel costs and stretched household budgets.

briefs.headline: Visa and Mastercard Enter Syria as U.S. Lifts Terror Designation
briefs.body: The two payment networks announced the launch of international card-processing services in Syria following Washington's removal of the country's terrorism designation. The development opens a new frontier for electronic payments in a market that has operated almost entirely outside the global financial system for years, and drew attention to the broader geopolitical reshaping underway across the Middle East.

briefs.headline: Family Offices Signal Equity Optimism Even as Breadth Remains Thin
briefs.body: Data from CNBC's Family Office Portfolio Tracker showed wealthy private investors maintaining a bullish stance on equities heading into the final stretch of summer. The positioning stands in some tension with Thursday's narrow market breadth — fewer than half the names in our universe closed higher — suggesting large allocators may be betting on index-level resilience rather than broad participation.
